articles.title: AI gave me spare time, and sprints don't know what to do with it
articles.excerpt: Ever since I started parallelizing a lot more of my work with AI, I've felt the need to go looking for side projects. Of course, I try to make sure those side projects are directly valuable to the com…
articles.body: Ever since I started parallelizing a lot more of my work with AI, I've felt the need to go looking for side projects. Of course, I try to make sure those side projects are directly valuable to the company. And that's led me to things like exploring potential refactors in some of our classes, speeding up certain scripts, investigating slowdowns in our APM, and looking into our testing infrastructure to see if I can help there. That's just me as a developer, sitting there and thinking, "How can I better help this company?" And I can definitely find plenty of valuable things to do, between what I see in the code and my general understanding of the company's mission, its direction, and what matters most to our clients right now. But even with that, my view is never the complete picture.
articles.author: Caio Andrade

articles.body: This week on X, two posts about vibe-coded sites landed next to each other. One founder launched a passive pre-launch scanner and claimed that half the people shipping with Cursor, Claude, and Lovable leak keys, expose .env files or source maps, or skip basic security headers. That is their number, not a measured one, and I would not quote it as a statistic. The other post was a warning that coding agents will obey any AGENTS.md they find, including one a random website dropped into your Downloads folder. Put them together and you get the uncomfortable version of "it works on my machine": it works on the internet, and the internet can read more of it than you think. You do not need a pentest to find the worst of it. Everything below is passive.

articles.title: Stop Trusting Third-Party JavaScript by Default: Add a Blast-Radius Limit
articles.excerpt: A page loads a familiar analytics or experimentation script. The browser connects to the provider's legitimate CDN, receives a file over HTTPS, and runs it with access to the page. Nothing in that seq…
articles.body: A page loads a familiar analytics or experimentation script. The browser connects to the provider's legitimate CDN, receives a file over HTTPS, and runs it with access to the page. Nothing in that sequence looks unusual. That is precisely why a compromised third-party script is such a powerful delivery path. On November 16, 2026, Report URI reported that malicious JavaScript reached visitors to 178 organizations through Optimizely Web. It found malicious code in 188 snippets among 1,611 distinct snippets it examined. The modified snippets still came from Optimizely's CDN, and the injected code appeared in customer Project JavaScript.

articles.body: How to model piecewise brackets, social contribution caps, and a 54-iteration binary search solver with zero backend dependencies. When a developer compares a full-time salaried role against an independent contracting rate, most back-of-the-envelope formulas use a flat multiplier like rate = (salary / 2080) * 1.30 . From a software engineering perspective, the reason that multiplier fails is that compensation and tax rules are piecewise non-linear state machines .

articles.title: Invalid Image URL in AI APIs: Debug Fetch Failures Before Retrying
articles.excerpt: Originally published by Tokenhot Team on 2026-11-14. The DEV edition was formatted with AI assistance. An image opening in your browser does not prove an AI API can read it. Your browser may have a lo…
articles.body: Originally published by Tokenhot Team on 2026-11-14. The DEV edition was formatted with AI assistance. An image opening in your browser does not prove an AI API can read it. Your browser may have a login cookie, the link may return a preview page, or the signed URL may expire before the service fetches the file. For an “invalid image URL” or “failed to download image” error, check five things in order: the request field, the unauthenticated download, the actual image bytes, the link's lifetime, and access from the service's network . Repeated generation requests won't repair a login page or a malformed input field. This guide uses Tokenhot's documented image routes where the request format matters. The download checks are general diagnostics, not a catalog of Tokenhot error codes.

articles.title: SQL Challenge : How to Find the Top 2 Highest-Paid Employees in Each Department Using ROW_NUMBER()
articles.excerpt: SQL Challenge #103: Find the Top 2 Highest-Paid Employees in Every Department Using ROW_NUMBER() Window functions are very useful in SQL interviews and real-world data analysis. They help us rank reco…
articles.body: SQL Challenge #103: Find the Top 2 Highest-Paid Employees in Every Department Using ROW_NUMBER() Window functions are very useful in SQL interviews and real-world data analysis. They help us rank records, compare values and solve problems that are difficult to handle with basic aggregate functions. In this SQL challenge, let's solve a common business requirement: finding the two highest-paid employees in every department. The Problem Suppose you have an "employees" table containing employee IDs, employee names, department IDs and salaries. You need to prepare a report that returns the top two highest-paid employees separately for each department. For example, if the IT department has five employees, your query should return only the two employees with the highest salaries in IT.

articles.body: SnipZen : Manage Your Code Snippets & Sync Your VS Code Environment Across Devices 🚀 Developers often reuse code snippets, switch between machines and spend time setting up their development environments again and again. What if we could make that process simpler? A few months ago, I collaborated with my friend to build SnipZen — a platform that helps developers manage, import, export and sync their code snippets and VS Code environment setups. I'm finally sharing this project with the developer community! 💡 Why SnipZen? We wanted to address a few common developer productivity problems: Manually transferring code snippets between machines. Losing track of useful reusable code. Reconfiguring VS Code extensions, settings and keybindings on new devices.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
articles.body: On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch
articles.excerpt: See the most epic photos from SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and historic launch tower catch.
articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.
articles.author: Josh Dinner

articles.body: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday , Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters . The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." articles.title: NASA Receives 16th Consecutive ‘Clean’ Financial Audit Opinion
articles.excerpt: For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion…
articles.body: Credit: NASA For the 16th consecutive year, NASA has received an unmodified, or “clean,” opinion from an external auditor on its fiscal year 2026 financial statements. The rating is the best possible audit opinion, certifying that NASA’s financial statements conform with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for federal agencies and accurately present the agency’s financial position. “Our responsibility at NASA is to be disciplined stewards of the resources entrusted to us by the American people while delivering on the missions they expect from this agency,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.

articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model
articles.excerpt: Just a day after SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket back at the launch pad for the first time ever, Elon Musk told us that the spacecraft will get even bigger.
articles.body: As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15).
